default_source: QNL institutional preservation evidence seed data
notes: Seed data and template for QNL-specific format evidence. Add future formats by copying a record, updating the format identifiers, and adding criterion-level claims. This is evidence for preservation-risk analysis, not a final risk decision or preservation action.

records.description: QNL treats standard PDF/PDF-A workflows as locally well-supported and low operational risk when files are not encrypted or DRM-protected.

claims.statement: PDF is treated at QNL as a documented and well-understood preservation/access format with broad tooling support.
PDF is widely encountered in QNL digital collections and user access workflows, making institutional handling routine.
Although PDF is not plain text, QNL has standard tools and workflows to characterize, inspect, render, and validate PDF files.
PDF can carry embedded descriptive and technical metadata, supporting preservation context when metadata is present and maintained.
QNL maintains tools capable of opening, validating, and normalizing ordinary PDF files without depending on a single proprietary workstation environment.
QNL has no known local licensing barrier that prevents preservation processing or access handling for ordinary PDF files.
Unencrypted PDF files are suitable for QNL ingest, validation, indexing, and migration workflows. Encrypted or DRM-protected PDF files should be treated as a separate risk case.
PDF can be structurally complex, but QNL has routine tooling and staff familiarity for managing that complexity in normal preservation workflows.
PDF compression and embedded resources are handled by QNL's standard validation and rendering toolchain for ordinary PDF files.
PDF can support text layers, tagging, bookmarks, and other accessibility-related features, although individual files still require quality assessment.
PDF is locally suitable for preserving and delivering document layout and page-level access copies in QNL services.
QNL currently maintains software capable of rendering, validating, and processing PDF files.
QNL digital preservation and curation staff have routine operational experience with PDF preservation and access workflows.
PDF is integrated into QNL ingest, characterization, preservation, and access workflows.
PDF storage and bandwidth demands are considered manageable within QNL's current preservation and access infrastructure.

records.description: QNL has no established institutional expertise or routine preservation workflow for netCDF; it should be treated as domain-specific scientific data requiring specialist review.

claims.statement: QNL has not yet documented a local assessment of netCDF specifications and preservation implications; specialist review is required before treating it as locally supported.
netCDF is domain-specific scientific data. QNL does not currently treat it as a routine high-volume institutional preservation format.
QNL staff cannot reliably inspect or interpret netCDF content without specialist scientific data tools and domain knowledge.
netCDF may include scientific metadata and structure, but QNL requires domain expertise to evaluate whether that metadata is sufficient for long-term understanding and reuse.
Opening, validating, and interpreting netCDF at QNL would require specialist scientific data libraries or tools that are not part of the current routine preservation workflow.
QNL has not completed a local licensing/IP assessment for netCDF preservation handling. This is not currently the main risk, but it remains unverified locally.
QNL has no current evidence that TPM or encryption is the main preservation issue for netCDF, but this has not been tested through a QNL ingest workflow.
netCDF should be treated as a structured scientific dataset format rather than a simple single-file access format; QNL needs specialist validation of structure and semantics.
QNL has not tested netCDF compression/chunking behavior or migration safety in local preservation workflows.
netCDF access is not a standard document/media accessibility problem; QNL would need a data-specific access and interpretation strategy.
QNL lacks local validation procedures to confirm that netCDF variables, dimensions, attributes, and data types are preserved and interpretable over time.
QNL would need domain review to understand whether netCDF conventions, metadata, and schemas are sufficient for preservation and reuse.
QNL does not currently maintain routine preservation software workflows for netCDF ingest, validation, rendering, or access.
QNL does not currently have established institutional expertise for preserving and assessing netCDF scientific datasets.
netCDF is not currently integrated into QNL's routine ingest, characterization, preservation, or access workflows.
QNL has not integrated netCDF-specific validation tooling into its preservation pipeline.
QNL cannot assess netCDF scale, storage, or bandwidth impact until candidate collections are profiled.
